q: Why did sales drop on 9 October?

problems: figures in no tool result and not one arithmetic step from them: 36,088

answer:
Yes — sales did drop on 9 Oct. Net sales were ₹53,880 on 2026-10-09 vs ₹90,962 on 2026-10-08 (a fall of 40.8%); versus the recent “usual” level the day is −39.5% (usual ≈ ₹89,086). This is a large one-day decline and matters because it was driven by far fewer orders, not lower traffic.

What changed, in order of impact:
- Orders fell sharply: 58 → 26 (−55.2%), which reduced sales by about ₹36,088. This is the single biggest driver of the drop.  
- AOV moved the other way: net AOV rose ₹1,568 → ₹2,072 (+32.1%), which offset some lost sales (+₹14,881) but not enough.  
- Ad spend was lower: ₹69,851 → ₹60,102 (−14.0%), but the diagnosis flags ad spend as an arithmetic component rather than a supported upstream cause.  
- Sessions did not fall (4,224 → 4,461, +5.6%); conversion rate collapsed 1.19% → 0.56% (−52.8%), so the funnel broke at conversion rather than traffic.  
- By ad: ad TH-222-WINGBIRD’s net sales fell from ₹8,931 → ₹1,101 and its orders 10 → 1; other ads moved in different directions (some rose).

What the analysis does and doesn’t say:
- The data decomposes exactly what changed (orders, AOV, costs, ad-spend components) and shows where the loss sat: orders / conversion rate.  
- It did not find a single upstream cause (no tested cause met the threshold). Sessions, ad spend and returns do not explain the drop on their own in the statistics the system ran.

Worth checking:
- Drill the drop by campaign_name / ad name and by landing page (conversion) to find where conversion collapsed (TH-222-WINGBIRD is a clear outlier to start with).
